title: fix(sse): stabilize SSE chunking/framing for partial JSON and delimiter ordering
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Fixes several edge cases in SSE streaming where partial JSON payloads and delimiter tokens could be emitted out-of-order, causing receivers to observe malformed or truncated JSON objects. Improves resilience and adds deterministic ordering guarantees for event/frame emission.
description:
Context: customers and internal tests started surfacing intermittent broken JSON objects when consuming SSE-based streaming responses. Root cause: the chunking/framing layer sometimes emitted delimiter events (partial JSON delimiter tokens, e.g. '

' or explicit separator events) before the final tokenized JSON chunk finished streaming, and the framing state machine allowed a race between tokenization and 'end-of-object' flush path. This manifested as partial JSON objects, duplicate delimiters, and occasional JSON parse errors in downstream OpenAI-compat clients.

This PR: stabilizes the SSE streaming framer and token/event ordering. Key changes: 1) make framing state machine deterministic by introducing an explicit frame-completion phase before delimiter emission; 2) ensure partial JSON chunks are buffered and emitted in order even when tokenization and network flush happen concurrently; 3) canonicalize delimiter semantics (single newline separator semantics) and add a toggle to support legacy double-delimiter behavior for older clients; 4) add additional observability (framing/sequence_id metrics and debug logs gated behind feature flag) to help triage future issues.

Checklist: [x] reproduce failing case in integration test harness; [x] unit tests for delimiter and ordering invariants; [x] integration test with OpenAI-compat adapter; [x] add metrics and feature flag; [x] update changelog and release notes.

Testing: added deterministic unit tests for ordering (framer_test.go) covering: partial JSON sequences across chunk boundaries, delimiter emission ordering, and recovery from mid-frame errors. Integration tests validate streaming through openai compatibility adapter and a small consumer harness that parses SSE payloads. CI showed an initial flaky integration test; added a deterministic wait/flush on the consumer side to make the test stable.

Related: ENG-4123 and ENG-4187 track broader streaming reliability work and a customer incident (SUP-8891). No API surface breaking changes; legacy double-delimiter mode can be enabled via feature toggle for canary.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on framing state transitions in pkg/runtime/sse/framer.go and the OpenAI compatibility adapter changes in pkg/api/openai/compat/stream_adapter.go. Logging additions are behind feature flag 'sse_framer_debug'.

review_comments: Diego Morales: The state machine change looks good; can we add a short comment describing the three-phase lifecycle (accepting, completion, delimiter-emission) so future readers don't forget the invariants?
Ava Chen: Added inline docs and a state diagram in framer.go per request. Also added a unit test that asserts the invariant across randomized chunk boundaries.
Priya Shah: Integration test is flaky locally for me the first time — I suspect a timing assumption in the consumer harness. Please make the consumer read loop resilient to small delays.
Ava Chen: Updated the harness to use a deterministic flush and retry up to 50ms; CI reran and passed consistently.
Riley Thompson: Approving pending a tiny lint fix and confirming the metrics are behind the feature flag. Logged LGTM once lint fixed.
Ava Chen: Addressed lint and gated metrics under 'sse_framer_debug'.
notes: This patch fixes a regression that started appearing after earlier batching optimizations. The legacy double-delimiter compatibility flag should be enabled only during canary for clients that require the old behavior. Monitoring: watch metric 'sse.framer.sequence_gap' and parse error alerts for 24h post-release.
consumer_impact: None expected for most clients. Clients parsing SSE into JSON objects should see fewer parse errors. Legacy clients relying on double-delimiter semantics can opt-in to legacy behavior via feature flag.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start streaming a large JSON object that emits tokens in small chunks. 2) Interrupt the stream emission boundary to force partial JSON chunks across network flushes. 3) Observe earlier behavior where delimiter sometimes came before final token (broken JSON). The updated framer preserves ordering and emits delimiter only after frame completion.
post_merge_actions: 1) Enable 'sse_framer_debug' for 10% of traffic for 48h to validate metrics. 2) Monitor 'sse.parse_errors' and 'sse.framer.sequence_gap' dashboards. 3) Roll out legacy_double_delimiter to 0% (off) by default.
changelog_entry: stability: Fix SSE streaming framing and partial JSON delimiter ordering to eliminate intermittent malformed JSON for streaming consumers (ENG-4123).
